text: Independent evidence corroborating the 2021 loss includes data from multiple sources. The University of Maryland's Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13) observed an 81.3-hectare tree-cover loss in 2021, which is 2.23% of the asset. The European Commission Joint Research Centre's Global Forest Cover 2020 dataset (GFC2020 V4) confirms that 98% of this area was mapped as forest in 2020. Additionally, Uruguay's Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries (MGAP) National forest cartography for 2021 identifies the affected area as planted forest, primarily consisting of Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda. These datasets collectively support the occurrence of the loss event in 2021.
